title: Encore - How to get unstuck with Adam Alter, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a winter break, so we're rerunning one of our favorite episodes
sentences.zh: 《心理学聊斋》要放寒假了，所以我们正在重播过去的一期最受欢迎的节目。

sentences.en: from the paSt. In June, I talked to psychologist Adam Alter about how to get unstuck when you're feeling stalled in a job, a relationship, or any other aspect of your life.
sentences.zh: 在六月份，我采访了心理学家亚当·奥尔特，探讨当你在工作、恋爱或生活的其他方面感到停滞不前时，该如何打破僵局。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoy this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期来自档案库的节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology, we'll be back in January with new episodes.
sentences.zh: 说到《心理学聊斋》，我们将在明年一月带着全新节目回归。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢收听。

sentences.en: All of us know the feeling of being stuck.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都体验过卡壳的感觉。

sentences.en: Maybe you're stuck in a job that feels unfulfilling or in a relationship that's making you unhappy.
sentences.zh: 也许你被困在了一份索然无味的工作中，或者一段让你并不快乐的亲密关系里。

sentences.en: Maybe you're stuck because you want to finish the novel you're working on or learn to speak another language
sentences.zh: 也许你被困住是因为你想写完正在创作的小说、想学会一门外语，

sentences.en: or turn your hobby into a business, but you just can't seem to make it happen no matter how many attempts you try.
sentences.zh: 或者想把兴趣爱好变成一门生意，但无论你尝试了多少次，似乎都无法实现。

sentences.en: So is getting stuck just an inevitable part of life?
sentences.zh: 那么，陷入困境只是人生中不可避免的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Are there things you can do to set yourself up for getting stuck less often?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么方法可以让你减少陷入僵局的频率？

sentences.en: How do you know when it's time to quit versus push ahead?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道什么时候该放弃，什么时候该坚持？

sentences.en: And when you do feel stuck, what practical tips can you take to get past the mental, emotional, and other hurdles standing in your way?
sentences.zh: 当你真的感到困顿不堪时，有哪些实用的建议能帮你跨越挡在面前的心理、情感以及其他障碍？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学聊斋》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Adam Alter, a professor of marketing at New
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是亚当·奥尔特博士，他是纽约大学斯特恩商学院的市场营销学教授，

sentences.en: York University's Stern School of Business and an affiliate faculty member in the NYU psychology department.
sentences.zh: 也是纽约大学心理学系的兼职教员。

sentences.en: He's a social psychologist with a particular interest in how subtle cues in the environment can affect human cognition and behavior.
sentences.zh: 他是一名社会心理学家，对环境中的微小暗示如何影响人类认知和行为表现出浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: He's the author of three books, including the New York
sentences.zh: 他著有三本书，其中包括《纽约时报》畅销书《不可抗拒：成瘾性技术崛起与俘获人心的商业逻辑》，

sentences.en: Times bestseller, Irresistible, The Rise of Addictive Technology and the Business of Keeping Us Hooked, which is about the perils of technology addiction.
sentences.zh: 该书探讨了技术成瘾的危害。

sentences.en: More recently, he has been studying how people and organizations get stuck and how they can get unstuck.
sentences.zh: 最近，他一直在研究个人和组织是如何陷入困境的，以及他们该如何摆脱困境。

sentences.en: His newest book, published in May, is called
sentences.zh: 他于五月出版的新书名为

sentences.en: Anatomy of a Breakthrough, How to Get Unstuck When It Matters MoSt. Dr. Alter has also written for the New
sentences.zh: 《突破的剖析：在至关重要时如何摆脱困境》。奥尔特博士还为《纽约时报》、

sentences.en: York Times, The New Yorker, and The Washington Post, among other publications, and has consulted with dozens of companies and organizations around the world.
sentences.zh: 《纽约客》和《华盛顿邮报》等媒体撰稿，并为全球数十家公司和组织提供过咨询。

sentences.en: Dr. Alter, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 奥尔特博士，非常感谢你今天作客我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me, Kim.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来，金。

sentences.en: I gave a few examples of different kinds of stuck just a moment ago, being stuck in work, in a relationship, or in some kind of a creative endeavor.
sentences.zh: 刚才我举了几种不同困境的例子，比如工作受阻、感情不顺，或者在某种创造性探索中卡壳。

sentences.en: Now, when you think about being stuck, what's the common thread that ties all of these experiences together?
sentences.zh: 现在，当我们思考“被困住”这件事情时，把所有这些经历串联起来的共同线索是什么？

sentences.en: I'm interested in particular kinds of stuckness.
sentences.zh: 我对特定种类的困境特别感兴趣。

sentences.en: I'm especially interested in protracted or chronic stuckness.
sentences.zh: 我尤其关注长期的或慢性的困境。

sentences.en: These are occasions where people feel stuck for sometimes months, sometimes years, sometimes even decades, or for sometimes, in some cases, their entire lives.
sentences.zh: 这些情况指的是人们有时会感到被困住数月、数年、甚至数十年，在某些情况下甚至是一生。

sentences.en: That's what I'm interested in.
sentences.zh: 这就是我感兴趣的地方。

sentences.en: But I'm also specifically interested in cases where we have some agency.
sentences.zh: 但我也特指那些我们还具有一定主观能动性的情况。

sentences.en: During the early days of the pandemic in 2020, a lot of us couldn't travel.
sentences.zh: 在2020年疫情初期，我们许多人都无法出行。

sentences.en: We couldn't do a lot of the things we wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 我们无法做很多自己想做的事情。

sentences.en: We were therefore stuck.
sentences.zh: 因此我们被困住了。

sentences.en: That wasn't as psychologically interesting to me as a case where we do have the power to act.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说，在心理学上的吸引力不如我们确实有能力采取行动的情况。

sentences.en: There is something we can do.
sentences.zh: 我们其实有事可做。

sentences.en: There aren't government regulations preventing us from doing a certain thing we want to be able to do.
sentences.zh: 并没有政府法规阻止我们去做我们想做的事。

sentences.en: It turns out the vast majority of these occasions of stuckness, where people feel they'd like to be in a different situation that
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在绝大多数这类困境中——即人们觉得希望改变现状，

sentences.en: often goes on for a long time, most of those cases, we do have some agency over.
sentences.zh: 而且这种情况往往持续很长时间——在大多数情况下，我们其实都具有一定的主观能动性。

sentences.en: I'm very interested in this book and in general, in my research, in trying to figure out how we can get unstuck from
sentences.zh: 在这本书中以及我总体的研究中，我非常感兴趣的是去弄清楚我们如何才能从

sentences.en: those situations that tend to plague us for long periods of time.
sentences.zh: 那些往往长期折磨我们的困境中摆脱出来。

sentences.en: How common is it to feel stuck?
sentences.zh: 感到被困住有多普遍？

sentences.en: I know you've done some surveys to study this.
sentences.zh: 我知道你做过一些调查来研究这个问题。

sentences.en: Does getting stuck happen to everyone, at least occasionally?
sentences.zh: 每个人都会遇到被困住的情况吗，至少偶尔会这样？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: Does it happen more to some people than others?
sentences.zh: 有些人比其他人更容易遇到这种情况吗？

sentences.en: I haven't really looked at individual differences in how often people are stuck, but I've been very interested in how common stuckness is in general.
sentences.zh: 我并没有真正研究过人们被困频率的个体差异，但我一直对困境普遍存在的程度非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: One of the surveys I've been running for several years now has looked at people around the world and asked them the simple
sentences.zh: 我这几年一直在进行的一项调查，针对世界各地的人们提出了一个简单的问题：

sentences.en: question, once I define what it is to be stuck, whether there's any area of their lives where they feel stuck.
sentences.zh: 在我定义了什么是“被困住”之后，询问他们生活中是否有任何领域让他们感到困顿。

sentences.en: What's fascinating to me is that the vast majority, I'd say over 90% of them, within
sentences.zh: 让我着迷的是，绝大多数人——可以说超过90%的人——在

sentences.en: 10, 15 seconds start typing a response.
sentences.zh: 10到15秒内就开始键入回答。

sentences.en: They're very quick to be able to draw to mind these occasions or instances or areas in which they feel stuck, which suggests that they're quite prominent.
sentences.zh: 他们能非常迅速地联想起这些经历、事件或感到困顿的领域，这表明这些感受非常突出。

sentences.en: They're top of mind.
sentences.zh: 它们占据了思维的前沿。

sentences.en: They're a big part of what it is to be alive.
sentences.zh: 它们是生而为人的一大重要部分。

sentences.en: I think of stuckness as ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 我认为困境是无处不在的。

sentences.en: You talk in the book about how people are more likely to get stuck in the middle of a project rather than at the beginning or at the end.
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到，人们更有可能在项目进行到中间阶段时卡壳，而不是在开始或结束时。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Yes, this is some interesting research that looks at goal pursuit and the relationship between goal pursuit and motivation.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一项有趣的研究，它着眼于目标追求以及目标追求与动机之间的关系。

sentences.en: What it basically suggests is that at the beginning of a task, you're energized, you're usually interested in what you're doing, you bring a lot of good resources to
sentences.zh: 它基本上表明，在任务开始时，你是充满活力的，通常对你正在做的事情感兴趣，你会投入大量好的资源

sentences.en: bear on the task.
sentences.zh: 来完成任务。

sentences.en: You can imagine any long task, any protracted goal where at the beginning, the fact that you're even starting it usually means that you have a little bit of wind behind your sails.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象任何长期的任务、任何持久的目标，在刚开始时，你甚至开始做这件事这一事实通常就意味着你顺风顺水。

sentences.en: That pushes you ahead.
sentences.zh: 这会推动你向前发展。

sentences.en: At the end of the task, as you can see the finish line, either metaphorically or literally in some cases, you get another burst of energy because you're drawn almost magnetically
sentences.zh: 在任务接近尾声时，当你看到终点线——无论是隐喻上的还是在某些情况下的字面意义——你会获得又一波能量，因为你几乎像被磁铁吸引一样

sentences.en: to that finish line.
sentences.zh: 冲向终点线。

sentences.en: For protracted goals, I liken it a bit to sailing across the ocean between North
sentences.zh: 对于长期的目标，我把它比作乘船横渡北美和欧洲之间的大洋，

sentences.en: America and Europe, that you're spending a huge period of time in the middle there between, say, New York and Southampton where you're unable to measure progress.
sentences.zh: 你在中间那段漫长的时间里，比如在纽约和南安普顿之间，你是无法衡量进展的。

sentences.en: If there is progress and there may well be progress, it's very, very hard to get a sense of that progress because there are no real signposts or markers in the middle of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 如果说有进展，而且可能确实有进展，也很难感受到这种进展，因为茫茫大海中没有真正的路标或标记。

sentences.en: Often in long protracted goals, goals, especially in the middle of those goals, you don't have the same sense of progress and that can be demotivating.
sentences.zh: 通常在漫长的目标中，特别是在这些目标的中间阶段，你没有那种明显的进展感，这会消磨动力。

sentences.en: There tends to be this quite predictable lull in motivation during the middle part of long protracted goals.
sentences.zh: 在漫长目标的中间阶段，往往会出现这种完全可以预见的动力低谷。

sentences.en: That's not just true of humans.
sentences.zh: 这不仅适用于人类。

sentences.en: It's true of lower order animals as well, but it's certainly very prominent in human behavior.
sentences.zh: 低等动物也是如此，但在人类行为中它无疑非常显眼。

sentences.en: Is one of the tricks to pace yourself?
sentences.zh: 其中的秘诀之一是调整自己的节奏吗？

sentences.en: Is that something that can help people not get stuck in the middle of something if they know that they're going to chunk the job down into discrete pieces?
sentences.zh: 如果人们知道要把工作拆分成独立的块，这能否帮助他们在做事的过程中不卡壳？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Part of it is pacing yourself.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于调整节奏。

sentences.en: There's a really interesting phenomenon known as teleo anticipation, which is literally the anticipation of the end.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常有趣的现象被称为“目的预期”，字面意思就是对终点的预期。

sentences.en: What we're supposed to do with protracted goals is to work out either explicitly or implicitly at the beginning of that process,
sentences.zh: 我们在面对长期目标时应该做的是，在整个过程开始时，无论是明确地还是隐含地计算出：

sentences.en: how much energy will I need in total and how should I best apportion that energy across the course of the goal?
sentences.zh: 我总共需要多少能量？我应该如何在整个目标推进过程中最好地分配这些能量？

sentences.en: That's a really difficult problem and there's often a lot of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常困难的问题，而且往往伴随着很多不确定性。

sentences.en: What you've described briefly there is another alternative, which is instead of just thinking of the goal as
sentences.zh: 你刚才简要描述的是另一种选择，那就是与其把目标看作

sentences.en: one big goal, you break it down or bracket it more narrowly into sub goals.
sentences.zh: 一个巨大的目标，不如把它拆分得更细，或者更窄地划分成子目标。

sentences.en: The beauty of that is that instead of thinking of it as one long goal with a very big middle, if you make those chunks small enough, you lose the middle, you eradicate the middle.
sentences.zh: 这样做妙就妙在，与其把它当成一个中间很长的单一目标，如果你把这些块切得足够小，你就会失去中间段，从而消灭中间段。

sentences.en: Then you have a start, you have a finish, you have a start, you have a finish, and you repeat that process.
sentences.zh: 然后你有了起点，有了终点，又有了起点，有了终点，你不断重复这个过程。

sentences.en: If you think about writing a book, for example, it's maybe a hundred thousand words, which is overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑写一本书，比如它可能由十万字组成，这让人望而生畏。

sentences.en: There's a big middle there.
sentences.zh: 中间有一大段很长的空白期。

sentences.en: But if you think of it instead as, say, a hundred periods of writing a thousand words each, the middle in each of those thousand word chunks is much smaller.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把它看作是一百个一千字的写作周期，那么每个千字小节里的“中间段”就短得多了。

sentences.en: You tend not to have such a pronounced lull.
sentences.zh: 你往往就不会经历那么明显的低谷。

sentences.en: You also talk in the book about what you call the creative cliff.
sentences.zh: 你还在书中谈到了你所说的“创意悬崖”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that term?
sentences.zh: 你这个术语是什么意思？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's actually, it's not the creative cliff so much as the creative cliff illusion.
sentences.zh: 所以其实与其说是创意悬崖，不如说是“创意悬崖错觉”。

sentences.en: And it's an illusion that people have that we believe that we become less creative over time when we're trying to think of creative solutions to a problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一种人们拥有的错觉：当我们试图想出一个问题的创新解决方案时，我们坚信自己会随着时间的推移变得越来越缺乏创造力。

sentences.en: So an example of this might be something like, there's a new soft drink company and you're working at a company and your job
sentences.zh: 所以一个例子可能是这样的：假设有一家新的软饮料公司，你在该公司工作，你的工作

sentences.en: is to come up with good slogans for this new soft drink company.
sentences.zh: 是为这家新软饮料公司想出好的口号。

sentences.en: If I said to you, do you think your best ideas will come in the first 10 slogans you come up with or in the next set of 10 between 11 and 20?
sentences.zh: 如果我对你说，你觉得你最好的创意会出现在你最先想出的10个口号里，还是在第11到第20个之间的下一组10个里？

sentences.en: And the vast majority of people say, well, the stuff that comes easily to me tends to come early.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人会说，嗯，那些很容易想到的东西往往出现得比较早。

sentences.en: It's going to be harder as I go along.
sentences.zh: 随着我继续做下去，事情会变得越来越难。

sentences.en: And I generally associate ease with skill, with fluency, with ability.
sentences.zh: 我通常把轻松等同于熟练、流利和能力。

sentences.en: And so just as with learning a language, the more fluent I am with the language, the easier it'll come to me.
sentences.zh: 因此，就像学语言一样，我对语言越流利，它就越容易自然流露。

sentences.en: And so I assume the same about creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以我也对创造力抱持同样的假设。

sentences.en: What turns out to be true though is the reverse, which is that it's when things start getting hard that your ideas become more creative.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明恰恰相反，当事情开始变得艰难时，你的点子才会变得更有创造力。

sentences.en: Instead of there being a cliff over which your creativity tumbles, you sort of lift off.
sentences.zh: 并非存在一个会让你的创造力跌落的悬崖，你反而是起飞了。

sentences.en: You lift off from the ground at the point where things start to get hard.
sentences.zh: 在事情开始变难的那一刻，你从地面起飞了。

sentences.en: And so we have this sort of classic problem in human psychology is misinterpreting the signals around us to
sentences.zh: 所以我们面临着人类心理学中的一种经典问题，即误解了周围的信号，

sentences.en: suggest that we should either quit or that we've already, our best is behind us.
sentences.zh: 暗示我们要么该放弃了，要么我们最好的时光已经过去。

sentences.en: And in this case, explicitly the reverse is true, where we tend to do much better with creative tasks only after they start to become difficult.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，事实完全相反，只有在创意任务开始变得困难之后，我们往往才能做得更好。

sentences.en: Is it also common for people to hit plateaus in life?
sentences.zh: 人们在生活中陷入平台期也很常见吗？

sentences.en: And is a plateau the same as being stuck or is it just a variant or are you just sort of cruising along at one steady level?
sentences.zh: 平台期和被困住是一回事，还是只是一种变体，亦或是你只是在某个平稳的水平上巡航？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So a plateau is really where the returns that you're getting from a particular strategy stop arriving or they shrink in size.
sentences.zh: 平台期实际上是指你从特定策略中获得的收益停止增长，或者收益缩减。

sentences.en: So this might be, for example, there's a very famous example of this looking at people who are sedentary and then they get an exercise regime and then
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是，举个非常著名的例子，观察那些久坐不动的人，然后他们开始制定锻炼计划，接着

sentences.en: they're tracked for a seven-year period.
sentences.zh: 对他们进行为期七年的追踪。

sentences.en: What you find is that these people tend to make gains for the first 12 to 18 months, but almost universally the same thing that they've been doing that was
sentences.zh: 你会发现，这些人在前12到18个月内往往会有所进步，但几乎无一例外，他们一直在做的事情——

sentences.en: really useful for 12 to 18 months becomes less useful beyond that.
sentences.zh: 在过去的12到18个月里真的很有用——在此之后变得不那么管用了。

sentences.en: So they need to change what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要改变自己的做法。

sentences.en: The same is true for learning and for memory and memorization techniques that we see a similar situation happening when you're, for example, trying to learn a language that if you
sentences.zh: 学习和记忆以及记忆技巧也是如此，当我们看到类似的情况发生时，比如你试图学习一门语言，如果你

sentences.en: keep using the same strategy, it becomes less effective over time.
sentences.zh: 一直使用相同的策略，随着时间的推移，它的效果会变得越来越差。

sentences.en: And that's an example of a plateau.
sentences.zh: 这就是平台期的一个例子。

sentences.en: So it could be that you hit a wall.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是你撞墙了。

sentences.en: That's one possibility.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可能性。

sentences.en: That's the sort of extreme version.
sentences.zh: 这是那种极端版本。

sentences.en: But the alternative is that just the marginal gains you get from further effort decline over
sentences.zh: 但另一种可能是，随着时间的推移，你通过进一步努力获得的边际收益递减，

sentences.en: time to the point where you're just not getting quite as much back, whereas formerly the same technique was really beneficial.
sentences.zh: 直到你的回报大不如前，而过去同样的技术其实是非常有益的。

sentences.en: So that's how I generally think of plateaus.
sentences.zh: 这就是我通常对平台期的理解。

sentences.en: They don't have to be that you stop making progress altogether, but you certainly slow down.
sentences.zh: 它们不一定意味着你完全停止了进步，但你的速度肯定放缓了。

sentences.en: Let's talk about some of the advice you offer in the book because there's quite a lot there and it's very good.
sentences.zh: 让我们来谈谈你在书中提供的一些建议，因为那里有很多内容，而且非常棒。

sentences.en: One thing you advise is to talk to other people when you're feeling stuck, especially to people who are unlike yourself.
sentences.zh: 你的建议之一是，当你感到困惑时，要与其他人交谈，尤其是与那些与你不同的人交谈。

sentences.en: Why is that helpful?
sentences.zh: 为什么这很有帮助？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a tremendous resource that humans have that really other animals do not have.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是人类拥有的一项巨大资源，而其他动物确实没有。

sentences.en: You know, we have a tremendous social network to draw upon when we're stuck.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们陷入困境时，我们可以利用一个巨大的社交网络。

sentences.en: And if you speak to people who are like you, who have the same background, perhaps the same
sentences.zh: 如果你和与你相似的人交谈，他们有着相同的背景、也许相同的

sentences.en: expertise, maybe they've trained the same way, maybe they grew up in the same place, maybe they have
sentences.zh: 专业知识，也许他们受过同样的训练，也许他们在同一个地方长大，也许他们有着

sentences.en: the same demographic characteristics, you'll find that they will magnify whatever you've been doing.
sentences.zh: 相同的人口统计特征，你会发现他们会放大你一直在做的事情。

sentences.en: So if you're doing something well, they will probably tell you to keep doing it or they'll help you keep doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你某件事做得很好，他们可能会告诉你继续做下去，或者他们会帮你继续做下去。

sentences.en: But if you're stuck, by definition, you might get more entrenched in your stuckness by speaking to people who are like you because they'll magnify that stuckness.
sentences.zh: 但如果你被困住了，根据定义，如果你和与你相似的人交谈，你可能会更深地陷入困境，因为他们会放大这种困顿。

sentences.en: The best thing you can do is you can speak to people who are either different from you, the technical term is non-redundant.
sentences.zh: 你能做的最好的事情就是和那些与你不同的人交谈——专业术语叫作“非冗余”。

sentences.en: In other words, there's no overlap.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，没有重叠。

sentences.en: Or you can talk to people who actively push back on your ideas if you're open to that.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你愿意接受的话，你可以和那些积极反驳你观点的人交谈。

sentences.en: And the value of that is instead of having 10 overlapping minds, if you speak to 10 people who all see life a little bit differently,
sentences.zh: 这样做的价值在于，与其拥有10个重叠的头脑，如果你和10个看待生活略有不同的人交谈，

sentences.en: you're getting 10 independent sources of wisdom.
sentences.zh: 你就会获得10个独立的智慧源泉。

sentences.en: And then your job really is just to comb through those 10 different sets of ideas and to figure out what works best for you.
sentences.zh: 那么你的工作其实就是仔细梳理这10套不同的想法，找出最适合你的方案。

sentences.en: And so the idea there, as with much of what I talk about in the book, is that quality and quantity are strongly related.
sentences.zh: 所以那里的核心理念——正如我在书中讨论的大部分内容一样——是质量和数量密切相关。

sentences.en: And so if you get more ideas, if you have more people sharing ideas that are distinct, you're more likely to find some good ones.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你获得更多的主意，如果你有更多的人分享不同的想法，你就更有可能找到一些好点子。

sentences.en: Another piece of advice that you offer, which seems to apply particularly to being stuck in a creative endeavor,
sentences.zh: 你提供的另一个建议，似乎特别适用于在创意探索中卡壳的情况，

sentences.en: is to take the pressure off yourself to come up with things that are entirely new and unique, and instead to think about recombining ideas.
sentences.zh: 那就是卸下“必须想出全新且独特的东西”的心理压力，转而思考如何重组各种想法。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is one of the ideas that I came across.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是我偶然发现的想法之一。

sentences.en: I love the arts in general, but I particularly love music.
sentences.zh: 我总体上很喜欢艺术，但我尤其喜欢音乐。

sentences.en: And I've always been really interested in this question that's now become a legal issue in a lot of cases, which is, are people stealing from others?
sentences.zh: 我一直对这个现在在许多案件中都变成法律问题的问题非常感兴趣，那就是：人们究竟有没有在抄袭他人？

sentences.en: Are artists stealing their ideas, their songs, their melodies, their chords, and so on from other artists who've written music in the past?
sentences.zh: 艺术家们是否在从过去创作过音乐的其他艺术家那里，窃取他们的创意、歌曲、旋律、和弦等等？

sentences.en: And when you speak to experts, they'll tell you that almost never does that happen.
sentences.zh: 当你和专家交谈时，他们会告诉你这种事几乎从未发生过。

sentences.en: It's very rare for someone to say, I'm going to rip off this other artist because it's often transparent.
sentences.zh: 很少有人会说：“我要抄袭这个别的艺术家，”因为这往往太明显了。

sentences.en: It leads them to hot water.
sentences.zh: 这会给他们带来麻烦。

sentences.en: It's not a good idea professionally.
sentences.zh: 从职业角度来看，这不是一个好主意。

sentences.en: And so I don't think that happens very often.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种情况并不常见。

sentences.en: But I think what does happen is we are constantly borrowing.
sentences.zh: 但我认为真正发生的是，我们一直在借鉴。

sentences.en: We're, you use the term recombining, which is a term that I use in the book.
sentences.zh: 我们，你用了“重组”这个词，这也是我在书中使用的术语。

sentences.en: We're essentially taking two unoriginal ideas, but putting them together in a way that is original.
sentences.zh: 我们本质上是拿两个并不原创的点子，但把它们以一种原创的方式组合在一起。

sentences.en: We're recombining them in a way that's new.
sentences.zh: 我们以一种崭新的方式将它们重组。

sentences.en: So I think true radical novelty is vanishingly rare in creative pursuits.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在创意追求中，真正彻底的新颖性是极其罕见的。

sentences.en: But I think what's much more common and what is often a better thing to strive for, a better aim to strive for is to say, I think what I want to do is find two things that
sentences.zh: 但我认为更常见、且往往更值得去追求的目标是：我想做的是找到两件

sentences.en: have never been combined in a particular way and combine them in that way and see if that brings me value.
sentences.zh: 从未以某种特定方式结合过的事物，然后以那种方式将它们结合起来，看看这能否带给我价值。

sentences.en: What's really interesting to me is as I was doing research for this book, I wanted to sort of figure out who is the closest to being radically original.
sentences.zh: 对我来说非常有趣的是，在为这本书做研究时，我想弄清楚究竟谁最接近彻底的原创。

sentences.en: And if we trace back far enough, could we find that their originality breaks down at a certain point?
sentences.zh: 如果我们追溯得够远，我们会不会发现他们的原创性在某个特定时间点会瓦解？

sentences.en: And one of the examples that comes up very often for people is Bob Dylan.
sentences.zh: 人们经常提及的一个例子就是鲍勃·迪伦。

sentences.en: A lot of musicians say Dylan's a genuine, true, radical original.
sentences.zh: 许多音乐家说迪伦是一个真正的、彻底的原创人物。

sentences.en: But if you look at Dylan's own words, and you look at where his music comes from, even Dylan, as original as he is, was cobbling together a whole lot of different styles.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看迪伦自己的话，看看他的音乐从何而来，你就会发现即使是迪伦，尽管他如此富有原创性，也一直在拼凑各种不同的风格。

sentences.en: And he himself recognized that so much of his work was building on the folk tradition, for example.
sentences.zh: 他自己也承认，他的许多作品很大程度上都是在民间传统的基础上构建的。

sentences.en: And so you do this with art, you can do it with filmmaking.
sentences.zh: 不仅艺术如此，电影制作也是如此。

sentences.en: It's just very, very rare to find radical originality.
sentences.zh: 要找到彻底的原创实在是太难太难了。

sentences.en: And so recombining elements tends to be the better way to go.
sentences.zh: 因此，重组各种元素往往是更好的选择。

sentences.en: Did you find any radical originals?
sentences.zh: 你找到过任何彻底的原创人物吗？

sentences.en: No, not really, to be honeSt. I think if you go back far enough, you do find the lineage of almost every idea in someone else's work.
sentences.zh: 说实话，并没有。我认为如果你追溯得够远，几乎每个创意的脉络都能在别人的作品中找到。

sentences.en: The person who invented the wheel or fire.
sentences.zh: 比如发明轮子或火的那个人。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm sure even before the invention of the wheel, there was someone pushing around something slightly oblong shaped.
sentences.zh: 是的，我敢肯定，甚至在发明轮子之前，就有人在推着某种形状略微椭圆的东西了。

sentences.en: And someone who invented the wheel saw that and said, hey, I've got an idea.
sentences.zh: 而那个发明轮子的人看到了这一幕，然后说，嘿，我有个点子。

sentences.en: And they may have thought it was original, but it was just an iteration, an evolution rather than a revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们可能觉得这很有创意，但这只是一种迭代、一种演变，而不是一场革命。

sentences.en: What other phenomenon that you talk about in the book has to do with pivoting?
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到的另一个现象与转向（pivoting）有关，是什么？

sentences.en: And you tell some really great stories about people who are engaged in looking for something.
sentences.zh: 你讲述了一些非常精彩的故事，主角们都在致力于寻找某些东西。

sentences.en: Your job is to maybe invent a drug and you never get there, but then suddenly you discover that something that you found was radically different, but marketable.
sentences.zh: 你的工作可能是发明一种药物，但你从未成功，然而突然之间你发现你偶然得到的东西虽然完全不同，却极具市场价值。

sentences.en: Can you talk about some of those examples?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈其中一些例子吗？

sentences.en: Because I think the examples you have throughout the book are really rich and interesting.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得你在全书中的例子都非常丰富和有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think what happens a lot of the time, if you're looking for something, if you're trying to make, say, it's a clinical drug that you're making, or you're searching for
sentences.zh: 我认为很多时候发生的情况是，如果你在寻找什么，如果你试图制造，比方说你正在研发一种临床药物，或者你在寻找

sentences.en: some form of originality or success, whether you're an entrepreneur or an artist, it doesn't
sentences.zh: 某种形式的原创性或成功，无论你是一个企业家还是一个艺术家，你正在做什么其实

sentences.en: really matter what you're doing, is you become very heavily invested in the thing that you're working on.
sentences.zh: 并不重要，重要的是你会对你正在做的事情投入极大的心力。

sentences.en: You pour your heart and soul into it.
sentences.zh: 你把全部心血都倾注在其中。

sentences.en: And the golfer, Sam Sneed, who is known for having the most beautiful swing of all time, described the process of swinging the golf club as cradling a bird.
sentences.zh: 高尔夫球手萨姆·斯尼德（Sam Sneed）以拥有史上最完美挥杆而闻名，他将挥杆击球的过程描述为像是在轻轻托着一只鸟。

sentences.en: You don't want to cradle it so lightly that it flies away, but if you cradle it with too much force, you end up crushing it.
sentences.zh: 你不能托得太轻让它飞走了，但如果你用力过猛，最后又会把它捏死。

sentences.en: And that's kind of how I think the best, most nimble minds think about their ideas, that you don't want to be too flighty.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这正是最优秀的、最敏捷的头脑看待他们点子的方式——你既不能太轻率、留不住想法，

sentences.en: You want to pursue the idea as far as you can, but you need to be open to the possibility that you're wrong or that a slight tweak would improve your returns dramatically.
sentences.zh: 你应当尽其所能地去追求这个点子，但你必须保持开放的心态，接受自己可能是错的，或者微小的调整就能极大地提升回报的可能性。

sentences.en: And that's what I kept finding over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这就是我不断发现的情况。

sentences.en: A lot of the cases that come up in the history of science are chemists who are exploring new drugs.
sentences.zh: 科学史上出现的许多案例都是化学家在探索新药。

sentences.en: And there are so many examples of chemists who, for example, accidentally some of the drug they were working
sentences.zh: 有这么多的化学家，例如，他们不小心把正在研究的一些药物

sentences.en: with got on their tongues and they tasted this substance and realized that A, it wasn't poisonous because they still were alive.
sentences.zh: 弄到了舌头上，他们尝了尝这个物质，然后意识到：第一，它没有毒，因为他们还活着；

sentences.en: And B, that it was really, really sweet.
sentences.zh: 第二，它真的非常非常甜。

sentences.en: And they didn't realize this.
sentences.zh: 而他们之前并没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And so a lot of the artificial sweeteners that have then made companies billions of dollars over the years come from these kind of accidental discoveries.
sentences.zh: 因此，多年来为公司带来数十亿美元收入的许多人工甜味剂，都源自这种偶然的发现。

sentences.en: Now, a lot of people are not receptive to that kind of serendipity.
sentences.zh: 现在，很多人对这种机缘巧合并不敏感。

sentences.en: But if you are, if you look for it, if you're always open to the idea that you might be wrong, there are certain people who are just very good at capitalizing
sentences.zh: 但如果你对它敏感，如果你去寻找它，如果你始终对“自己可能是错的”这一想法保持开放，就会发现有些人非常擅长利用、

sentences.en: on, seizing on these moments.
sentences.zh: 抓紧这些时刻。

sentences.en: And it's not just about chemistry.
sentences.zh: 这不仅关乎化学。

sentences.en: It's about art as well.
sentences.zh: 这也关乎艺术。

sentences.en: And it's about business.
sentences.zh: 这也关乎商业。

sentences.en: And you see a lot of these cases of people pivoting in ways that ended up being very, very profitable for them.
sentences.zh: 你会看到很多这样的案例：人们以最终被证明对他们非常、非常有利的方式进行了转向。

sentences.en: I want to talk for a moment about the idea of writer's block.
sentences.zh: 我想花点时间谈谈“作家之块”（灵感枯竭）的概念。

sentences.en: I would imagine that all of our listeners have heard the term and maybe have experienced it, whether they were
sentences.zh: 我想我们的所有听众都听说过这个词，也许都经历过，无论他们是

sentences.en: in college and they had to write a term paper, or maybe in their jobs today where you have an assignment to produce a big report.
sentences.zh: 在大学里必须写期末论文，还是在如今的工作中需要完成一份重大报告的任务。

sentences.en: Is there really such a thing as writer's block?
sentences.zh: 真的有所谓的“作家之块”这种东西吗？

sentences.en: Or is it just that people can't get started?
sentences.zh: 还是说这只是人们无法开始行动？

sentences.en: And what are the techniques that can get you unstuck in that kind of a situation?
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下，有哪些技巧能帮你摆脱困境？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's so funny, because this is a term that I always took for granted.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太有趣了，因为这是一个我一直觉得理所当然的词。

sentences.en: I assumed that it was a concept that was well recognized, that everyone agreed, yes, there was something called writer's block, or at least some version of it.
sentences.zh: 我以为这是一个广为人知的概念，大家都同意确实有一种叫作作家之块的东西，或者至少是它的某种版本。

sentences.en: But it's such a polarizing term, because you speak to some writers, and they say, Oh, I have no idea what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个两极分化的词，因为你跟一些作家交流时，他们会说：“哦，我完全不知道你在说什么。

sentences.en: That's a ridiculous concept.
sentences.zh: 那是个荒谬的概念。”

sentences.en: And I just sit down and I write.
sentences.zh: “我坐下来就能写。”

sentences.en: And then they're very firm about that.
sentences.zh: 而且他们对此非常坚定。

sentences.en: And then there are other writers who say, Oh, yeah, every day is writer's block until it's not.
sentences.zh: 然后还有其他作家会说：“哦，是的，每天都是灵感枯竭，直到灵感到来。”

sentences.en: And then you have writers who for a decade don't write anything.
sentences.zh: 还有一些作家十年什么也写不出来。

sentences.en: So it's a fascinating sort of, there's a lot of variance in how we experience it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个令人着迷的现象，我们在经历它时存在着很大的差异。

sentences.en: One of the things I like best, though, is the attitude of Jeff
sentences.zh: 不过，我最喜欢的态度之一来自杰夫·

sentences.en: Tweedy, who is the front man, the songwriter, the singer for the band, the rock band Wilco, and also himself a writer, he writes a lot of books and things like that.
sentences.zh: 特维迪（Jeff Tweedy），他是摇滚乐队威尔科（Wilco）的前台、词曲作者兼主唱，同时他自己也是个作家，写过很多书之类的内容。

sentences.en: So he's a Renaissance man who his trade is really creativity, he has to wake up every day and be creative.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个全才，他的职业本质上就是创意，他必须每天醒来都充满创意。

sentences.en: And like any human being who's open and honest, he says, I don't wake up every day wanting to be creative.
sentences.zh: 和任何坦诚面对自己的普通人一样，他说：“我并不是每天醒来都渴望拥有创意。”

sentences.en: You know, my best creative force is not brought to the work that I'm doing every day.
sentences.zh: “你知道的，我最好的创造力并没有倾注到我每天在做的工作中。”

sentences.en: But he doesn't have the luxury, like a newspaper writer who needs to write a column, you don't always have the luxury of having writer's block.
sentences.zh: 但他不像需要写专栏的报社记者那样拥有奢侈的选择，你并不总是有遭遇灵感枯竭的奢侈权利。

sentences.en: So what he has done that I think is really interesting is he, he thinks of his creative ideas as as though what he has is essentially a body of water.
sentences.zh: 所以他采取的做法我觉得非常有趣：他把自己的创意点子想象成基本上是一个水体。

sentences.en: And the clean crystal clear water is at the bottom of this body, but on top of it sits a layer of muck.
sentences.zh: 清澈见底的水在这个水体的底部，但在它上面覆盖着一层污垢。

sentences.en: And the good ideas are covered by this muck.
sentences.zh: 而好的点子就被这些污垢覆盖着。

sentences.en: And the muck is, you know, I'm tired, I can't get motivated.
sentences.zh: 这些污垢就是：我很累，我没有动力。

sentences.en: And it's the sort of sense of writer's block.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种灵感枯竭的感觉。

sentences.en: And he talks about pouring out the bad ideas metaphorically.
sentences.zh: 他谈到要用隐喻的方式把不好的点子倒出来。

sentences.en: And the way he does that is he'll sit at his computer, or he'll sit with a pad and paper, or he might sit at his keyboard or his
sentences.zh: 他这样做的方法是：他会坐在电脑前，或者拿着纸笔，或者坐在键盘或

sentences.en: guitar, you know, thinking about how he's going to write a song.
sentences.zh: 吉他前（想着自己要怎么写一首歌）。

sentences.en: And he'll say to himself, the best thing I can do right now, if I don't want to be stuck is to act doesn't really matter what the action looks like.
sentences.zh: 他会对自己说：“我现在能做最好的事，如果我不想卡壳的话，就是去行动，行动看起来是什么样并不重要。”

sentences.en: But I need to act because then, you know, by definition, I'm not stuck.
sentences.zh: “但我需要行动，因为这样一来，根据定义，我就没有卡壳。”

sentences.en: And so what he does is he says, in those moments for say 10 or 15 minutes at the beginning of the day, I'm going
sentences.zh: 所以他所做的就是，在那些时刻——比如一天开始时的10到15分钟里——他会

sentences.en: to lower my usually very high threshold for what's acceptable to the ground, and say anything is good, anything is acceptable for the purposes of getting the ball rolling.
sentences.zh: 把通常对自己极高的可接受标准降到地面，并告诉自己：“任何东西都是好的，为了让事情运转起来，任何东西都是可以接受的。”

sentences.en: And so what he'll say to himself is something like, what's the worst musical phrase I could write right now?
sentences.zh: 所以他会对自己说这样的话：“我现在能写出的最烂的音乐乐句是什么？”

sentences.en: Or what's the worst passage that I could write?
sentences.zh: “或者我能写出的最烂的段落是什么？”

sentences.en: And the good news is, if you're if you've been doing this for long enough, it's very easy to do a bad job.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，如果你做这行够久了，要写得很烂是一件非常容易的事。

sentences.en: But it turns out to be better than doing no job at all.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这总比什么都不做要好。

sentences.en: And that's what he's found that it really does seem to propel him forward.
sentences.zh: 这就是他发现的方法，它确实能推动他向前发展。

sentences.en: And then after he's done that for a bit, he gets into the groove.
sentences.zh: 在他这样做了小一会儿之后，他就进入状态了。

sentences.en: And so for him, there is essentially no writer's block once he uses that tactic.
sentences.zh: 因此对他来说，一旦他使用了这个策略，基本上就不存在什么灵感枯竭了。

sentences.en: And that's how I often think of writer's block that as long as you act, even if the action is sideways, you'll get over writer's block.
sentences.zh: 这就是我经常看待灵感枯竭的方式——只要你采取行动，哪怕行动是歪打正着，你也能克服灵感枯竭。

sentences.en: It seems like one reason people get stuck these days, especially when they're trying to make a decision, is because there's so much information
sentences.zh: 似乎人们如今常常卡壳的一个原因，特别是当他们试图做出决定时，是因为有太多信息

sentences.en: available at our fingertips right now.
sentences.zh: 触手可及。

sentences.en: You give the example in the book of trying to decide what kind of car to get.
sentences.zh: 你在书中举了试图决定买什么车的例子。

sentences.en: What advice do you have for people when they get analysis paralysis because there's too much information to sift through?
sentences.zh: 当人们因为有太多信息需要筛选而陷入分析瘫痪时，你有什么建议？

sentences.en: I think it's tempting to think of ourselves as a particular kind of decision maker.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们很容易把自己看作某种特定类型的决策者。

sentences.en: Often we see our decision making as a sort of expression of wisdom.
sentences.zh: 通常我们把自己的决策视为一种智慧的表达。

sentences.en: I make good decisions.
sentences.zh: 我能做出好的决定。

sentences.en: I'm a good decision maker.
sentences.zh: 我是一个好的决策者。

sentences.en: I make the right decision.
sentences.zh: 我总是做出正确的决定。

sentences.en: I think a better way to think about decision making is to think of every decision in terms of its gravity.
sentences.zh: 我认为思考决策的一个更好方法是根据其严重性来评估每一个决定。

sentences.en: And to ask yourself, is this a case where I need to be absolutely right?
sentences.zh: 并问问自己：这是那种我必须绝对正确的案例吗？

sentences.en: I need to make the very best decision, which is known as maximizing.
sentences.zh: 我需要做出最好的决定，这被称为最大化（maximizing）。

sentences.en: I maximize the outcome.
sentences.zh: 我使结果最大化。

sentences.en: Or is this a case where I can, the alternative is satisficing, where I basically say there's a hurdle.
sentences.zh: 或者，这是那种我可以使用“满意策略”（satisficing）的情况，即我基本上设定了一个门槛。

sentences.en: I need to get over that hurdle.
sentences.zh: 我需要跨过这个门槛。

sentences.en: And as long as I come up against an option that's good enough, that's acceptable here.
sentences.zh: 只要我遇到一个足够好、在这里可以接受的选项就行。

sentences.en: I don't need to find the perfect option.
sentences.zh: 我不需要找到完美的选项。

sentences.en: So there may be some areas of your life, for example, picking a partner or deciding whether
sentences.zh: 因此，你生活中的某些领域可能需要这样，例如挑选伴侣，或者决定

sentences.en: they have children or deciding which house to buy or which town to live in or country to live in.
sentences.zh: 是否要孩子，或者决定买哪栋房子、在哪个城镇或哪个国家生活。

sentences.en: Those are big decisions and I think they warrant a lot of care and attention.
sentences.zh: 这些都是重大决定，我认为它们值得付出大量的关注和心思。

sentences.en: And so you should feel to some extent paralyzed by that decision and you should take a long time making it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某种程度上，你应该对那个决定感到有些瘫痪，并且应该花很长时间去做出它。

sentences.en: But if you're standing at a wall of sodas at the supermarket and you're spending four hours trying to decide
sentences.zh: 但如果你站在超市的苏打水货架前，花了四个小时试图决定

sentences.en: whether to go between Coke and Pepsi, that's a good case for satisficing.
sentences.zh: 是在可口可乐和百事可乐之间二选一，那这就是采用满意策略的好例子。

sentences.en: And I think most decisions we make during the day, even if there are hundreds of them, 99% of them probably fall in the satisficing camp.
sentences.zh: 我想我们白天做出的大多数决定，即使有数百个，其中99%可能都属于满意策略的范畴。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of research on satisficers versus maximizers, people who generally say good enough is good enough versus perfection is the only thing I'm looking for.
sentences.zh: 关于满足者与最大化者——那些通常认为“差不多就行”的人与只寻找“完美”的人——有很多研究。

sentences.en: If you hunt for perfection, you will be less happy, both with what you choose, but also in life in general.
sentences.zh: 如果你追求完美，你不仅对你的选择会不那么快乐，对整体生活也会如此。

sentences.en: And so I think learning to distinguish these cases where it's essential to make the right decision from the ones where it
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为学会区分那些必须做出正确决定的情况，以及那些其实

sentences.en: doesn't actually matter that much is a really useful life philosophy.
sentences.zh: 无伤大雅的情况，是一种非常有用的人生哲学。

sentences.en: I hope that comes as a relief to some of our listeners.
sentences.zh: 我希望这能让我们的听众松一口气。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Since artificial intelligence is all over the news today, I'd want to ask you if you've given any thought to how AI might help us get unstuck.
sentences.zh: 既然人工智能如今铺天盖地，我想问问你是否考虑过人工智能如何能帮我们摆脱困境。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking about a conversation I had with a colleague just the other day who had a work assignment where he had to synthesize a bunch
sentences.zh: 我想到了前几天我和一位同事的对话，他有一项工作任务，必须综合一堆

sentences.en: of information and come up with recommendations.
sentences.zh: 信息并提出建议。

sentences.en: He didn't have a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 他没有太多时间。

sentences.en: He didn't see any immediate answers.
sentences.zh: 他看不到任何现成的答案。

sentences.en: So he turned to chat GPT, poured in the source information, and it spit out what he needed.
sentences.zh: 于是他求助于 ChatGPT，把原始信息喂了进去，它就吐出了他需要的东西。

sentences.en: So do you think generative AI is going to be another answer to getting unstuck?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为生成式人工智能会成为摆脱困境的另一个答案吗？

sentences.en: Yes, very much so.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常会。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, as an educator, I'm now stuck because half of the assignments I've assigned for the last 20 years are no longer viable.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，作为一名教育工作者，我现在也卡壳了，因为我过去20年布置的一半作业现在都不可行了。

sentences.en: But my situation aside, I think it's a tremendous resource.
sentences.zh: 但抛开我的处境不谈，我认为这是一项巨大的资源。

sentences.en: And I think where it does its best work is, you know, we talked a little bit earlier about this idea of consulting others who are a bit different from you for advice and when you
sentences.zh: 我认为它发挥最好作用的地方在于，我们刚才讨论过向与你稍有不同的人寻求建议的想法，当你在

sentences.en: feel stuck.
sentences.zh: 感到卡壳时。

sentences.en: And I think chat GPT functions as essentially the collected wisdom of millions of different agents that are out there in the world because it's combing what's available on the
sentences.zh: 我认为 ChatGPT 的功能本质上就是世界上数百万个不同智能体的集体智慧结晶，因为它在梳理互联网上

sentences.en: internet.
sentences.zh: 可用的内容。

sentences.en: So generative AI for me is this great unsticking force that can be used as the kind of first step in the process, whatever the process might be.
sentences.zh: 因此，对我而言，生成式 AI 是一种伟大的解困力量，可以用作这个过程的第一步，无论这个过程是什么。

sentences.en: So I think that's usually where we get stuck.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这通常是我们卡壳的地方。

sentences.en: It's going from zero to one.
sentences.zh: 那就是从零到一的过程。

sentences.en: And an example of this is if I'm sitting and struggling to write the beginning sentence of a chapter or the beginning paragraph of a chapter, and I'm writing a book,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果我坐着苦思冥想，想写出一章的开头句子或开头段落，而我正在写一本书，

sentences.en: which is something I've done a few times now, and I've often been stuck at the beginning of a chapter.
sentences.zh: 这也是我已经做过几次的事情，我经常在一章的开头卡壳。

sentences.en: It's a difficult thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这是一件很难做到的事。

sentences.en: One thing you can do, and I have done this with chat GPT occasionally, is you can say to it, I'm writing a book chapter.
sentences.zh: 你可以做的一件事——我偶尔也会对 ChatGPT 这样做——就是对它说：我正在写一本书的一章。

sentences.en: This is what the chapter is about.
sentences.zh: 这就是本章所探讨的内容。

sentences.en: You can give it a brief description.
sentences.zh: 你可以为它写一个简短的描述。

sentences.en: Tell me five different ways that you could write this chapter.
sentences.zh: 告诉我五种编写本章的不同方法。

sentences.en: You could begin the chapter.
sentences.zh: 你可以从这一章的开头写起。

sentences.en: Now, it doesn't mean you're plagiarizing, but what it's doing is it's getting you to think about some different options the way you might if you'd spoken to five of
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你在抄袭，而是让你去思考一些不同的选项，就像你和五位最优秀的作家朋友交流过，他们对你说：嗯，我会这样做。

sentences.en: your best writer friends and they said, well, here's what I would do.
sentences.zh: 你的最优秀的作家朋友，他们说，嗯，我会这样做。

sentences.en: Instantly, without having to check schedules and so on, you have this device or this platform that's telling you, here are five different ways to do it.
sentences.zh: 瞬间，你无需核对时间表等等，就能拥有这样一个工具或平台，告诉你：这里有五种不同的做法。

sentences.en: And the nice thing about chat GPT is if you say to it, let's imagine that the last thing you said was wrong, or let's improve on what you just did.
sentences.zh: ChatGPT 的妙处在于，如果你对它说：假设你刚才说的是错的，或者让我们改进一下你刚才的表现。

sentences.en: It'll do that for you.
sentences.zh: 它会为你做到这一点。

sentences.en: And so you can push it and prod it in different directions.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以从不同的方向去推动和引导它。

sentences.en: So I find it a tremendous brainstorming partner for that early phase where you feel stuck and where you're trying to move from zero miles an hour to maybe 10 miles an hour.
sentences.zh: 因此，我发现它是早期阶段一个极好的头脑风暴伙伴，在那个阶段你会感到卡壳，试图从每小时零英里推进到大约每小时十英里。

sentences.en: From 10 to 60, if that's what your goal is, you might have to do that on your own, but it gets you started.
sentences.zh: 从每小时10英里到60英里，如果那是你的目标，你可能得靠自己去实现，但它能帮你开个好头。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a moment about the role of fear in being stuck.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈恐惧在陷入僵局中所起的作用。

sentences.en: Do people sometimes get stuck just because they're afraid of change or of the unknown?
sentences.zh: 人们有时会因为害怕改变或未知而陷入困境吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this survey that I've been running on people around the world, one of the questions I ask is, tell me what it feels like as you think about being stuck.
sentences.zh: 我在世界各地的人群中开展的这项调查中，我提出的问题之一是：告诉我，当你想到陷入僵局时，那是一种什么样的感觉。

sentences.en: And it's not surprising, I think, that the emotions they feel are negative.
sentences.zh: 我认为，他们感受到的情绪是负面的，这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: And fear comes up quite often.
sentences.zh: 恐惧出现的频率相当高。

sentences.en: Anxiety comes up quite often.
sentences.zh: 焦虑出现的频率也相当高。

sentences.en: There's a real sense of isolation and loneliness, despite the fact that it seems near universal.
sentences.zh: 尽管这种现象似乎近乎普遍存在，但人们仍有一种强烈的孤立感和孤独感。

sentences.en: It's often hidden from us that others are stuck as well.
sentences.zh: 我们常常意识不到其他人也陷入了困境。

sentences.en: And I find one of the best ways to get over that fear of feeling stuck is to shine sunlight on this idea that being stuck is universal.
sentences.zh: 我发现，克服对陷入困境的恐惧的最佳方法之一，就是揭示一个事实：陷入困境是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: And in fact, the beginning of the book, I spent quite a long time trying to figure out whether there were some
sentences.zh: 事实上，在书的开头，我花了不少时间去寻找，看是否存在一些经典的例子：

sentences.en: classic examples of tremendously successful people from the outside, who once you look at the process
sentences.zh: 从外表看极其成功的人，一旦你深入了解那些不为人知的过程，就会发现

sentences.en: that was hidden from the world, you find, turns out they were very, very afraid, very stuck, very uncomfortable until they weren't.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在他们豁然开朗之前，他们曾感到非常非常害怕、非常卡壳、非常不安。

sentences.en: And you find this with some of the biggest businesses in the world.
sentences.zh: 你在世界上一些最大的企业身上也能发现这一点。

sentences.en: I talk about Amazon and Airbnb.
sentences.zh: 我谈到了亚马逊和爱彼迎（Airbnb）。

sentences.en: You find it with some of the most successful artists.
sentences.zh: 你在一些最成功的艺术家身上也能找到这种现象。

sentences.en: I specifically focus at the beginning of the book on Brie Larson, the actress who won an Academy Award for Best Actress.
sentences.zh: 我在书的开头专门聚焦于布丽·拉尔森（Brie Larson），这位曾荣获奥斯卡最佳女主角奖的女演员。

sentences.en: And I'm yet to find someone who says, in all honesty, I was never stuck.
sentences.zh: 我至今还没遇到过一个人，他能诚实地说：我从未陷入过困境。

sentences.en: It was always easy.
sentences.zh: 一切总是轻而易举。

sentences.en: It was plain sailing.
sentences.zh: 一切都是一帆风顺。

sentences.en: It was not an issue for me at all.
sentences.zh: 这对根本我来说根本不是问题。

sentences.en: And so yes, going back to your question, I think fear is a very big factor that prevents people from moving forward.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，回到你的问题，我认为恐惧是阻碍人们前进的一个非常大的因素。

sentences.en: But so much of that comes from the sense that this is a sort of unique experience that I'm going through.
sentences.zh: 但很大程度上源于这样一种感觉：我正在经历的是一种独一无二的体验。

sentences.en: And once you get past that, it usually feels, in my experience, quite liberating and people do move forward.
sentences.zh: 一旦你跨过了这个坎，以我的经验来看，通常会感到相当解脱，人们也会继续前进。

sentences.en: When a person has been stuck on something for a long time, how do they know when it's time to quit versus whether they should continue to try to push through?
sentences.zh: 当一个人在某件事上卡住很长时间时，他们怎么知道什么时候该放弃，什么时候该继续咬牙坚持？

sentences.en: Is there some kind of a cost benefit analysis that people could do in such cases?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，人们是否可以做某种成本效益分析？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a very interesting and important question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常有趣且重要的问题。

sentences.en: It's one of the big questions that comes up.
sentences.zh: 这是经常出现的大问题之一。

sentences.en: In the book, I think I push quite firmly on the idea of persevering in general, because I think a lot of the research suggests there's a lot of value
sentences.zh: 在书中，我认为我对普遍坚持的观点持相当坚定的支持态度，因为我认为很多研究表明，

sentences.en: to persevering beyond the point where things get difficult.
sentences.zh: 在事情变得困难之后仍然坚持下去，具有巨大的价值。

sentences.en: There are also some phenomenal books, including a book by Annie Duke called Quit, which is about the opposite.
sentences.zh: 还有一些非凡的书籍，其中包括安妮·杜克（Annie Duke）所著的《放弃》（Quit），这本书讲的则是相反的道理。

sentences.en: How do you know when to stop?
sentences.zh: 你如何知道什么时候该停止？

sentences.en: And obviously, a wise assessment suggests that you can't always push forward and you can't always quit.
sentences.zh: 很显然，明智的评估表明，你不能一味地向前冲，也不能一遇到困难就放弃。

sentences.en: You need to know how to distinguish the two.
sentences.zh: 你需要知道如何区分这两者。

sentences.en: One of the useful pieces of advice that I've come across from people who seem to find the middle ground quite well is they will describe a sense of
sentences.zh: 我从那些能够很好地找到中间平衡点的人那里得到了一条很有用的建议，他们会描述一种

sentences.en: convergence on an endpoint that they desire.
sentences.zh: 向他们所期望的终点靠拢的感觉。

sentences.en: So if you're learning a language or a skill or you're trying to produce a creative idea or you have a business or you're trying out a career or you're
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你正在学习一门语言、一项技能，或者正试图产生成果、创办企业、尝试一项职业，又或者在大学里尝试一个新专业，无论是什么，你都可能会遇到一些困难。

sentences.en: trying a new major in college, whatever it might be, you'll probably run into some hardship.
sentences.zh: 你不能一遇到困难就放弃。

sentences.en: You can't quit at the first sign of hardship.
sentences.zh: 这是许多研究所表明的观点。

sentences.en: That's what a lot of the research suggests.
sentences.zh: 但如果你所做的一切只是苦苦挣扎，而且你觉得自已并没有向着某个有前途、有回报、让你感觉良好、能带给你所期望的情感回报的目标靠拢，那么在某个时刻，你确实需要放弃。

sentences.en: But if all you're doing is slogging through the process and you don't feel like you're converging
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以做的一件事——有时有一个客观的标准可以帮你做到这一点——

sentences.en: on something promising, rewarding, that makes you feel good, that brings you the emotional returns you're looking for, then at some point you do need to quit.
sentences.zh: 但你可以做的一件事是问自己：随着时间的推移，我离目标更近了吗？

sentences.en: And so one of the things you can do, sometimes there's an objective standard that helps you do this.
sentences.zh: 我在不断逼近目标吗？

sentences.en: But one thing you can do is to ask, am I getting closer to the goal over time?
sentences.zh: 我当前的技能水平或经验与我希望达到的理想状态之间的差距是在缩小，还是保持不变，甚至在变大？

sentences.en: Am I converging?
sentences.zh: 一旦这个差距开始变大，并且你觉得离自己想去的地方越来越远，我认为你就有了充分的理由去放弃。

sentences.en: Is the gap between my current skill level or my experience now and where I'd like to be shrinking or is it staying the same size or is it even getting larger?
sentences.zh: 但我认为，把放弃看作是一个空洞的概念是没有多大意义的。

sentences.en: And once it starts getting larger and you feel like you're getting further and further from where you want to be, I think you start to make a good case for quitting.
sentences.zh: 对我和来说，关键总是：你放弃是为了转向什么？

sentences.en: But I think the idea of quitting as an empty idea doesn't make much sense.
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: For me, it's always, what are you quitting to?
sentences.zh: 因此，在我的经验中，当我经历不同的进程并决定不做某事时，你能做的最好的事情，就是真正为下一件事做好排期，无论在什么情况下都尽可能做到这一点，特别是当它是一项职业或创意事业时。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 现在，除了学术工作之外，你还为许多公司和组织提供咨询服务。

sentences.en: And so in my experience, when I've moved through different processes and when I've decided not to do something, the best thing you can do is really to line up the next
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你给他们的建议是否类似于你给个人关于如何摆脱困境的建议？

sentences.en: thing and wherever possible, especially if it's a professional or creative endeavor.
sentences.zh: 大体上是相似的。

sentences.en: Now, in addition to your academic work, you do a lot of consulting with companies and organizations.
sentences.zh: 在书中，我在很大程度上关注个人，但我也专门讨论了组织、管理以及营销问题。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if the advice you give them is similar to the advice that you give to individuals in terms of how to get unstuck.
sentences.zh: 我认为，许多理念都是以领导力为导向的。

sentences.en: It's broadly similar.
sentences.zh: 你如何组建一个团队？

sentences.en: In the book, I focus on individuals to a large extent, but I also talk about organizations and management and marketing problems specifically.
sentences.zh: 你如何组建一个智囊团，以最大化地提高组织摆脱困境的机率？

sentences.en: A lot of the ideas, I think, are leadership oriented.
sentences.zh: 因此，有些理念我认为

sentences.en: How do you put together a team?
sentences.zh: 与商业决策息息相关，也许比日常生活更甚。

sentences.en: How do you put together a brain trust so that you maximize the chance of an organization unsticking?
sentences.zh: 但我总是发现，你知道的，我认为我们心理学家随着时间的推移学到的最大技能之一，就是有用的理念有着广泛的应用。

sentences.en: So there are some ideas that I think
sentences.zh: 而你能做的最好的事情，就是去弄清楚它们适用于哪里。

sentences.en: are germane to business decision making, maybe more than everyday life.
sentences.zh: 通常它们的适用范围比你的直觉所暗示的还要广泛。

sentences.en: But I always find, you know, I think one of the big skills that we psychologists learn over time is that useful ideas have a lot of applications.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是很多理念，举个例子，如果我要组建一个团队，并且我正在努力弄清楚应该把哪类员工纳入这个团队。

sentences.en: And the best thing you can do is try to figure out where they apply.
sentences.zh: 你可能会问的另一个问题，也就是个人的版本可能是：我正在努力组建一个值得信赖的人的群体，当我感到不知如何继续前行时，我可以向他们求助。

sentences.en: And often they apply more broadly than your instincts might suggeSt. And so I think a lot of the
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在职场以及日常生活中组建团队的规则是相通的。

sentences.en: ideas even, so here's an example, if I'm putting together a team, and I'm trying to work out what sort of employees to put on that team.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为你可以从商业理念中学到巨大的知识。

sentences.en: Another question that you might ask, the individual version of that might be, I'm trying to put together a group of trusted people that I can turn to when I feel
sentences.zh: 而且，商业理念也从作为一个在世界上探索的个体人类这一本质中获益良多。

sentences.en: like I don't know how to move forward.
sentences.zh: 我们还有没有讨论过、你想在今天留给听众的其他建议？

sentences.en: And it turns out the same rules about composing that team at the workplace and in life in general hold.
sentences.zh: 我想我要说的一点是，我们在童年时期——我有一个五岁和一个七岁的孩子——童年充满了好奇心。

sentences.en: And so I think you can learn a tremendous amount from the business ideas.
sentences.zh: 我们发现世界是一个充满好奇的地方。

sentences.en: And also the business ideas, I think, gain a lot from just what it is to be an individual human being navigating the world.
sentences.zh: 我们提出了大量的问题。

sentences.en: Is there any other advice that we haven't discussed that you'd want to leave with our listeners today?
sentences.zh: 我们极少对得到的第一个、第二个或第三个答案感到满意。

sentences.en: I think one thing I'll say is we, in childhood, I have a five-year-old and a seven-year-old, and in childhood, there's a lot of curiosity.
sentences.zh: 因此我们不断向前探索。

sentences.en: We find the world a curious place.
sentences.zh: 孩子们对他们得到的答案永远不会满足。

sentences.en: We ask a huge number of questions.
sentences.zh: 在从童年到成年的某个时期，这种心态发生了转变。

sentences.en: We're very rarely satisfied by the first, second, or third answers we get.
sentences.zh: 我们开始认为常识之所以成为常识是有原因的。

sentences.en: And so we push forward constantly.
sentences.zh: 成年人不会提出那么多问题。

sentences.en: And kids are never satisfied with the answers they get.
sentences.zh: 你看到别人在做什么，就会认为那是正确的方法，而小孩子可能会问：为什么会这样？

sentences.en: At some point between being a child and being an adult, that shifts.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，有些成年人天生就是这样，我称他们为实验主义者。

sentences.en: We start to assume that common wisdom is common wisdom for a reason.
sentences.zh: 这是一种质疑一切的哲学，他们会想，通过正确的实验，会不会有更好的方法。

sentences.en: Adults don't question that much.
sentences.zh: 我有没有更好的方法与我爱的人沟通？

sentences.en: You see other people doing something, you assume it's the right way where a child might say, why is that?
sentences.zh: 我有没有更好的方法在职场中工作？

sentences.en: And it turns out there are some adults who are natural, I call them experimentalists.
sentences.zh: 我甚至有没有更好的、更具体的方法来学习弹奏某首钢琴曲或画某幅画？

sentences.en: It's a sort of philosophy of questioning everything and wondering whether with the right experiment, there might be a better way.
sentences.zh: 任务本身其实并不重要。

sentences.en: Is there a better way for me to communicate with my loved ones?
sentences.zh: 但我在其中一章中谈到了这些惯常的实验主义者，以及这种做法如何为其中一些人释放出巨大的潜力。

sentences.en: Is there a better way for me to work in the workplace?
sentences.zh: 我谈到了一位奥运会游泳运动员，他通过本质上提出“大家都在游仰泳的方式并不是最好的方式”这种观点，在那种熟练水平下成为了一名奥运会游泳运动员。

sentences.en: Is there a better way for me even narrowly to learn how to play a particular piano piece or paint a particular painting?
sentences.zh: 他开创了一种全新的技术。

sentences.en: It doesn't really matter the task.
sentences.zh: 在其他领域也有这样的人。

sentences.en: But one of the chapters I talk about these people who are chronic experimentalists and how for some of them, it unlocks tremendous potential.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为这是一种非常宝贵、极其宝贵的生活态度，它能让我们保持年轻，并让我们保持开放的心态，或者说让我们对普遍做得更好的潜力保持开放。

sentences.en: I talk about an Olympic swimmer who learned to be an Olympic swimmer at that level of proficiency by essentially saying, hey, the way
sentences.zh: 我认为，防止自己一开始就陷入困境的最佳方法之一，就是永远对自己说：哦，是的，这开始让人觉得有点卡壳了。

sentences.en: everyone else is swimming, the backstroke is not the best way.
sentences.zh: 它的运行方式并不如我所愿。

sentences.en: He pioneered a completely new technique.
sentences.zh: 我想我需要考虑其他的替代方案。

sentences.en: And there are other people in other domains too.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常实用的建议。

sentences.en: So I think that's a really valuable,
sentences.zh: 接下来你有什么计划？

sentences.en: valuable approach to the world that keeps us a young and be makes us open or keeps us open to the potential to do better in general.
sentences.zh: 除了摆脱困境，你还在研究什么？

sentences.en: And I think it's one of the best ways to prevent yourself from getting stuck in the first place is to always say, oh yeah, this is starting to feel a little bit sticky.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's not working the way I'd like.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在研究一大堆的想法。

sentences.en: I think I need to consider alternatives.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我在书中也提到了这一点，我有一份名为“研究想法”的文件，还有另一份名为“书籍想法”的文件。

sentences.en: And that's, I think, a very useful piece of advice.
sentences.zh: 它们本质上是二十年来积攒下来的有趣想法，这些想法要么是自己想到的，要么是在世上偶然遇到的。

sentences.en: And what's next for you?
sentences.zh: 我需要花上一百辈子的时间才能真正把它们全部付诸实践。

sentences.en: What else are you working on besides stuckness?
sentences.zh: 所以，目前我全心投入到这本书中，以及探讨我们如何在许多不同情境下摆脱困境的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，我确信我会重新审视那些文件，并找出接下来要做什么。

sentences.en: So I'm constantly working on a whole lot of ideas.
sentences.zh: 好的，奥尔特博士，我要感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: And what they essentially are is 20 years worth of interesting ideas that have either come to me or that I've come across in the world.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来，金。

sentences.en: It would take me a hundred lifetimes to actually pursue all of them.
sentences.zh: 我真的非常享受。
